tools.name: list_items
tools.description: List Rollbar items (deduplicated errors) for the project, optionally filtered by status, level, environment or a search string

status.description: Optional item status to filter by (default is Rollbar's own, which includes active items)

level.description: Optional minimum-severity level to filter by

environment.description: Optional environment name to filter by (e.g. production)

query.description: Optional free-text search matched against the item title

page.description: Page number, 1-based (default 1). Rollbar fixes the page size itself

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: Get one Rollbar item by its item ID, with status, level, occurrence counts and first and last seen timestamps

item_id.description: Rollbar item ID, the numeric `id` from list_items (not the per-project `counter`)

tools.name: list_deploys
tools.description: List deploys recorded for the Rollbar project (revision, environment, who deployed it, start and finish times)

page.description: Page number, 1-based (default 1). Rollbar fixes the page size itself

tools.name: top_active_items
tools.description: Get the Rollbar items with the most occurrences recently (the noisiest errors right now), with their per-period counts

environment.description: Optional environment name to restrict the report to (e.g. production)

needs_review: Rollbar access tokens are PER PROJECT and per scope, so this connector is scoped to one project by the credential itself, not by a tool input. A `read` scope token is what these four calls need; a `write` or `post_server_item` token will be refused by the API. There is deliberately no project_id input: the token picks the project.

Every Rollbar response is enveloped as {"err": 0, "result": ...}, so every pick carries `err` through. Rollbar can answer 200 with a non-zero `err`, and dropping it would shape a refusal into an empty list and read as 'no items' (a silent-fallback falsehood).

top_active_items answers with `result` as a BARE ARRAY of {item, counts} pairs, so its pick uses the `result[]` array form and flattens the nested item fields; the other list tools nest their arrays under result.items / result.deploys.

list_items and list_deploys expose `page` rather than a limit because the Rollbar list endpoints take a page number and fix the page size themselves; the clamp helper is used on page (default 1, cap 100) purely to keep a caller from requesting an absurd offset. top_active_items is the one endpoint with a genuine count argument, so item_count is clamped to default 20 / max 50.
One request per tool (v1 limit) means no automatic paging: a caller pages by passing `page` back in, and the connector never loops.

Field presence is taken from the Rollbar API reference, not from a live 2xx: no Rollbar project token was held, so the proof below covers wiring only, never payload shape. Fields absent from a real payload simply drop out of the shaped result rather than appearing as nulls.

get_item takes the item `id`, which is the account-wide identifier, not the per-project `counter` shown in the Rollbar UI. The counter lookup is a different endpoint (/api/1/item_by_counter/{counter}) and is not exposed here.
